flags.note: Post 3 presents only the three best-performing holdings (+94%, +71%, +58%) over a self-selected 12-month window as proof of what the strategy 'can deliver,' with no total composite return in the post. That is a subset-of-positions presentation without the total portfolio it was extracted from (C8), and the winners-only framing is also a fair-and-balanced concern (C4). The cited code is imprecise but the text is genuinely reviewable.

Composite inception is 1/1/2012, so ~14 years of record exists, yet only a 1H-2026 stub and a 3-year annualized figure are shown versus the index. Required 1-, 5- and 10-year results are absent from both the post and the disclosure block (C3), and the truncated window selection raises C4. Returns are stated net, so C2 is satisfied; the period presentation still warrants review.

The quoted sentence is itself the risk disclosure, not an unbalanced benefits claim. It states that one bad decision costs more than in a 150-stock fund, that the portfolio can look nothing like the market for long stretches, and that the strategy is not right for everyone; the disclosure block adds that concentrated portfolios can be more volatile than diversified ones. C9 is already satisfied by this very text.

Exact duplicate of flag 3 - same quoted sentence, same C9 code, same rationale. Dismissed for the same reason: the passage is the balancing risk language the checklist asks for, not a benefits statement lacking it. No separate reviewer time warranted.
